title: Vesper and the Oath
premise: Ines Montrose, a bone-carver who hears the dead, has survived ten years in the city of Corvane by selling charms too small to be called magic — until a dying stranger presses a map into her hands and dies whispering about a door out of Vesper, a country that was erased from every record after its fall. The map marks seven thresholds across a land where the dead remember what the living were forced to forget, and Ines discovers she is one of the last who can open them. Hunted by the Warden's inquisitors and shadowed by Tam, the stranger's vengeful sister, she must choose between using her gift to survive alone or risking everything to carry Vesper's exiled dead home. At the final threshold beneath the drowned capital, Ines learns the door out was never an exit at all but a way back — and by opening it she surrenders her own name to the country that no longer exists, becoming its memory so its people can become real again.
about_author: Sable Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing confiscated letters from border towns before turning to fiction. She writes about places that history tried to delete, and the stubborn people who refuse to be forgotten.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet her in Corvane's night market, carving a charm from a dead woman's finger-bone while the woman's ghost dictates the words. A routine sale, a careful life, and the constant hum of voices only she can hear. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; she has made survival an art of staying small.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A bleeding man collapses into her workshop at closing time, pursued by someone wearing a Warden's grey. He presses an oilskin-wrapped map into her hands and makes her swear to carry it north before dying on her floor. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility; the oath binds her more tightly than any law.

chapters.title: Grey Coats in the Market
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Inquisitors sweep the market asking after a bone-carver; Ines burns her stock and hides among the dead whose bones she keeps, learning their silence can shield her. She decides to flee rather than hang. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; the first step out of a ten-year hiding place.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Say
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with interludes of the map itself speaking in dead voices. On the road north she deciphers the first threshold mark and realizes the map is written in the memories of the fallen country of Vesper — a name that makes listeners flinch or lie. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread; knowledge is now a target on her back.

chapters.title: Tam
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The stranger's sister ambushes Ines on the causeway, certain the bone-carver murdered her brother for his map. They fight; the dead intervene on Ines's behalf, and Tam, shaken, agrees to travel with her — to watch her, she says. Emotional beat: hostility edged with grief; two survivors circling each other.

chapters.title: The First Threshold
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At a ruined tollhouse they find the first door: a seam in the air only Ines can hear. Opening it costs her a memory — her mother's face — and shows her a vision of Vesper whole and burning. Emotional beat: awe and loss entwined; the price of survival becomes literal.

chapters.title: Roadside Justice
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. They rescue a family of Vesperan refugees from a tithe-gang, and Tam executes the gang leader against Ines's objections. Their argument about justice outside the law cracks something open between them. Emotional beat: moral friction; both women are right, and it nearly breaks the alliance.

chapters.title: The City That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They reach a town officially recorded as never having existed, where everyone over forty remembers it differently than the ledgers do. An old ferryman gives them passage and a warning: the Warden himself once came from Vesper. Emotional beat: uncanny dislocation; the ground truth of the world shifts underfoot.

chapters.title: The Warden's Ear
chapters.summary: Warden Casimir's POV. We enter the antagonist: a former Vesperan who helped erase his own country and now hunts the map to finish the job. He interrogates a captured inquisitor and learns the bone-carver hears the dead — the one ability that can reopen what he sealed. Emotional beat: cold, wounded purpose; he believes he is saving the world from a wound.

chapters.title: Voices in the Deep Water
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Crossing the flooded valley, the drowned dead of Vesper's capital call to Ines so loudly she nearly walks into the water. Tam pulls her back and, in the aftermath, finally tells her how her brother found the map — and what he promised their mother. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared danger; trust begins to outweigh suspicion.

chapters.title: The Second and Third Doors
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Two thresholds stand close together; opening both in one night strips away Ines's memories of her craft, leaving her unable to carve. She must decide whether a self without its art is still herself. Emotional beat: identity crisis at the story's midpoint; the theme of price made flesh.

chapters.title: A Country of Exiles
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. They shelter with a hidden community of Vesperans who have kept their language alive in secret for a decade. For one night there is music, real bread, names spoken aloud. Emotional beat: warmth and fragile hope; a glimpse of what they are fighting for, and what erasure actually steals.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Well
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. One of the exiles sells their location to the Wardens for his children's safety. The raid scatters the community; Ines escapes with the map but leaves people behind screaming her name. Emotional beat: guilt and rage; the cost of being known, and the impossibility of clean hands.

chapters.title: Casimir Offers a Bargain
chapters.summary: Warden Casimir's POV, then Ines's. Captured briefly, Ines is offered a deal: her freedom and Tam's in exchange for destroying the map. Casimir reveals the erased country was erased deliberately — it had opened something that should have stayed shut. Emotional beat: doubt weaponized; the villain's argument lands harder than expected.

chapters.title: What Ines Buried
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Recovering with Tam in the hills, Ines admits the truth she has hidden since chapter two: the dying stranger didn't choose her at random. Her grandmother was Vesperan, and the doors answer her blood. Tam's fury and forgiveness arrive in the same breath. Emotional beat: confession and reckoning; identity as inheritance, not choice.

chapters.title: The Fourth Door Opens Wrong
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Rushed and hunted, they force a threshold prematurely. What comes through is not memory but hunger — a fragment of whatever Casimir sealed long ago. They barely seal it again, and Ines understands why the country was buried. Emotional beat: horror and humility; the enemy may not be entirely wrong.

chapters.title: The Long March to the Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, short scenes. The remaining exiles join them, a ragged procession toward the drowned capital as winter closes in. Casimir's forces harry them; the dead of Vesper march invisibly alongside. Emotional beat: grim momentum; a funeral march that slowly becomes a homecoming.

chapters.title: The Drowned Capital
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Beneath the floodwaters lies the last threshold: the original door, vast and patient, guarded by the ghosts of those who closed it — including, Ines realizes, her grandmother. The dead ask her the question the whole book has been building toward: is a country worth what it will cost you? Emotional beat: confrontation with legacy; love and duty pulling opposite ways.

chapters.title: Casimir's Last Stand
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV dissolving into chaos. He arrives to stop the opening, and in the confrontation reveals he sealed the door to imprison not Vesper but the thing beneath it — and reopening the country risks freeing it. Tam holds him off while Ines descends. Emotional beat: tragic collision; two people protecting the same world in opposite ways.

chapters.title: The Door Out Is the Way Back
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the threshold, Ines grasps the truth: the door was never an escape route but a restoration, and it demands a keeper — a living memory to anchor the country's return. She offers her name, her carved bones, her collected selves. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into meaning; the climax of identity and price.

chapters.title: Vesper, Remembered
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The waters recede; the land rises; the exiles walk into streets that remember them. Casimir, broken, chooses exile rather than execution — justice outside the law, administered by the people he wronged. Tam stands at the shore holding the map, now blank. Emotional beat: catharsis and grief braided together; victory that does not feel simple.

chapters.title: The Bone-Carver's Silence
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, coda. Months later, in a Vesper rebuilding itself, Tam visits a quiet workshop where a woman carves charms and no longer hears the dead — except, sometimes, one voice that sounds like her own. Ines doesn't remember the oath, but she keeps it anyway. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; what we give up survives in what we leave behind.
